I strongly support a government ban on the sale of new petrol cars by no later than 2030. Real Hope, Real Change means acting now so young people inherit a secure future, not runaway climate chaos and crushing fuel bills. Fossil-fuel cars lock us into dirty, expensive systems that line the pockets of big oil while families struggle at the petrol pump. A 2030 ban, paired with public investment, puts Britain back in control: affordable, clean public transport, abundant charging on our streets, and a massive home insulation and retrofit programme so people can get around and live comfortably without rising costs.

This isn’t about taking choices away — it’s about widening them. Free or low-cost public transport for young people, grants for EVs for low-income households, and properly funded local buses and trains give communities practical options. We’ll create thousands of local green jobs in manufacturing, charging infrastructure, and retrofitting homes. For the Common Good, banning new petrol cars by 2030 is a fair, necessary step toward Fairer, Greener Communities and a secure future for everyone.

I utterly oppose any government plan to ban the sale of new petrol cars by 2030. This is the latest example of the out-of-touch Westminster “Green Blob” imposing costly ideology on ordinary people. For working families, farmers and small business owners a petrol ban means an enormous hit: higher upfront costs for electric cars, unreliable charging in rural areas, and yet more excuses to hike taxes and fines. Our towns and villages aren’t ready — many roads and homes lack chargers, and the electricity grid is already creaking. This isn’t progress, it’s punishment.

The real winners are global elites and foreign manufacturers, not British drivers. Rather than forcing everyone into expensive, impractical alternatives, we should stop the War on Drivers: scrap green levies that jack up bills, invest in British energy and charging infrastructure, and let consumers choose. Don’t let Net Zero technocrats decide how we live and work. Scrap the 2030 petrol car ban and put common-sense, affordable policies back in charge — Restoring Britain’s Power and Prosperity.

I strongly support a government ban on the sale of new petrol cars by no later than 2030. This is practical, urgent and fair — and it’s about delivering real hope and real change for communities across Britain. Rapidly shifting to electric and zero‑emission vehicles will cut household fuel bills, clean up toxic air outside schools and hospitals, and slash the emissions driving the climate and cost‑of‑living crises. But a ban must come with policies that protect people, not leave them behind.

That means massive public investment in affordable electric vehicle infrastructure, electrifying buses and trains under public ownership, and scrappage and retrofit grants targeted at low‑income households and key workers. It means guaranteeing good green jobs in communities hit by the transition and insulating homes so families aren’t worse off.

A 2030 ban, combined with social support and public provision, is a step toward fairer, greener communities — putting people and planet before corporate profit and building a secure future for everyone. For the common good.

But a ban alone won’t do it: we must pair it with massive investment in public transport, safe cycling and walking infrastructure, and rapid electrification of our rail network so people have real alternatives.

Crucially, the transition must be fair. That means grants and interest-free loans for low-income households to switch to electric vehicles where needed, a roll-out of accessible charging points in every town and council estate, and public ownership of the national grid and charging network so profits are reinvested in communities. Fossil fuel companies and private utilities shouldn’t be allowed to cash in while families bear the cost. A 2030 ban, backed by public investment and social justice, is Real Hope, Real Change — a secure future for everyone.

They want to tell you what to drive, when to drive it and how to live your life — all because a handful of Westminster mandarins demand virtue-signalling headlines. I oppose any government ban on the sale of new petrol cars by 2030. It is an out-of-touch, ideological diktat that will hit working people hardest: harder to replace a reliable family car, higher prices at the forecourt as green levies and compliance costs are passed on, and fewer affordable options for tradespeople, rural families and small businesses who depend on petrol vehicles every day.

This isn’t about climate compassion — it’s about imposing expensive technology before the UK has the charging infrastructure, battery capacity or manufacturing base to deliver it affordably. The result? Net Zero becomes Net Poverty: fewer choices, more expense, and a country that punishes hard work. Scrap this ban. Instead, focus on pragmatic measures: boost British energy and battery production, cut green taxes on fuel, and invest in real, affordable charging and fuel alternatives so people can choose — not be bullied — into a green future. Restore common sense. Stop the war on drivers.

It is an out-of-touch, ideological diktat that will hit working people hardest: harder to replace a reliable family car, higher prices at the forecourt as green levies and compliance costs are passed on, and fewer affordable options for tradespeople, rural families and small businesses who depend on petrol vehicles every day.

This isn’t about climate compassion — it’s about imposing expensive technology before the UK has the charging infrastructure, battery capacity or manufacturing base to deliver it affordably. The result? Net Zero becomes Net Poverty: fewer choices, more expense, and a country that punishes hard work. Scrap this ban. Instead, focus on pragmatic measures: boost British energy and battery production, cut green taxes on fuel, and invest in real, affordable charging and fuel alternatives so people can choose — not be bullied — into a green future. Restore common sense. Stop the war on drivers.

I strongly oppose a government ban on the sale of new petrol cars by 2030. This is London- and Brussels-style dogma dressed up as climate virtue-signalling — and it comes with a real price tag for ordinary people. Punishing working families, tradespeople, farmers and small businesses with an arbitrary deadline will force them to buy expensive electric cars they neither want nor can easily charge, while the same Westminster elites jet about pretending they’ve saved the planet.

Electric vehicles are not a universal solution: charging infrastructure in rural Britain is woeful, batteries degrade, and replacement costs are high. Banning petrol cars strips freedom of choice and hits those who rely on vehicles for their livelihoods. Instead of dictating from Whitehall, ministers should focus on expanding domestic energy, cutting green levies that drive up costs, investing in rural charging where it makes sense, and allowing technology to evolve naturally. Scrap the 2030 ban — put common sense and people’s pockets first. Scrap Net Zero to Cut Energy Bills. Net Zero is Net Poverty.

Punishing working families, tradespeople, farmers and small businesses with an arbitrary deadline will force them to buy expensive electric cars they neither want nor can easily charge, while the same Westminster elites jet about pretending they’ve saved the planet.

Electric vehicles are not a universal solution: charging infrastructure in rural Britain is woeful, batteries degrade, and replacement costs are high. Banning petrol cars strips freedom of choice and hits those who rely on vehicles for their livelihoods. Instead of dictating from Whitehall, ministers should focus on expanding domestic energy, cutting green levies that drive up costs, investing in rural charging where it makes sense, and allowing technology to evolve naturally. Scrap the 2030 ban — put common sense and people’s pockets first. Scrap Net Zero to Cut Energy Bills. Net Zero is Net Poverty.

I strongly support a government ban on the sale of new petrol cars by no later than 2030. This is Real Hope, Real Change — a practical, fair step that tackles the climate emergency and cuts household bills together. Electric vehicles are now cheaper to run and produce far fewer emissions; shifting away from petrol reduces air pollution around schools and hospitals, protecting our children’s lungs and easing pressure on the NHS.

But this must be done for the common good, not to entrench corporate profit. A 2030 ban should come with public investment to make the switch affordable: free or subsidised electric buses and trains, grants and accessible financing for low-income drivers, widespread public charge points, and support for council-led car clubs. We should prioritise insulation, cleaner local transport, and training for workers in battery and EV maintenance so communities benefit from new green jobs.

Fairer, Greener Communities means no one is left behind in the transition. Ban new petrol cars by 2030 — and fund it so it’s a secure future for everyone.
